newsitem.title: CANADA: Imasco off as Philip Morris slips.
newsitem.headline: Imasco off as Philip Morris slips.

text.p: Shares of Imasco Ltd slipped in brisk trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday after Morgan Stanley said it cut its earnings estimate for Philip Morris Cos.

By midday, Imasco was off C$0.25 at C$33.85 with more than 771,000 trading. In New York, shares of tobacco and consumer packaged goods maker Philip Morris shares were off 1/4 at US$113 in a turnover of almost 800,000 shares.

Jacques Kavafian, analyst with Research Captial Corp, told Reuters that Imasco's share price tends to follow trends set by big U.S. tobacco makers. Imasco's Imperial Tobacco unit is Canada's largest cigarette maker.
"Imasco tends to follow, but with a lag. If Philip Morris goes down five percent, Imasco might go down two percent," Kavafian said.

Kavafian said that if Montreal-based Imasco should slip to near C$30 over the next few weeks, he will change his recommendation on the stock to buy from hold on the strength of its tobacco and financial services operations.
"It's a first-rate liquid company with a lot of cash. I like its prospects going forward because it will have a lot of free cash flow from 1998," he said.
